title: SBI Q1 Profit Jumps 10% to Rs 21,121 Crore on Strong Loan Growth, Shares Rise
excerpt: India's largest lender beats analyst estimates as corporate credit and retail loans power an 18.6% surge in gross advances.
body:
• State Bank of India posted Q1 FY27 net profit of Rs 21,121 crore ($2.22 billion), beating analyst estimates of Rs 19,102 crore.
  • Gross loan growth hit 18.63%, driven by 18.05% corporate credit expansion and 15.15% retail loan growth.
  • Net interest income rose nearly 15% to Rs 46,992 crore, with domestic NIM expanding 7 basis points to 3%.
  • Asset quality improved with gross NPAs falling to 1.47% from 1.49% in the previous quarter.

State Bank of India reported a 10.2% jump in quarterly net profit to Rs 21,121 crore ($2.22 billion) for the three months ended June 30, comfortably beating analyst estimates of Rs 19,102 crore, according to LSEG data compiled by Reuters. Shares of India's largest lender rose over 3% on Friday following the results.

Loan Growth Drives Earnings

Credit growth has been robust across Asia's third-largest economy as firms borrow amid rising working capital needs and households make a beeline for consumption and gold-backed loans. SBI's gross advances surged 18.63% year-on-year, with corporate credit expanding 18.05% and retail personal loans growing 15.15%.

Net interest income — the difference between interest earned on loans and paid on deposits — grew nearly 15% to Rs 46,992 crore. The domestic net interest margin expanded 7 basis points from the previous quarter to 3%, a notable improvement at a time when many Indian banks have seen margin compression.

"Credit growth has been robust as firms borrow amid rising working capital needs and households make a beeline for consumption and gold-backed loans."

— Reuters

Asset Quality Holds Steady

The bank's asset quality improved slightly, with gross non-performing assets falling to 1.47% of total loans from 1.49% three months earlier. Deposits rose 9.73% from a year ago, reflecting continued confidence in the state-run lender's balance sheet.

The results come a week after the Reserve Bank of India held its benchmark repo rate steady at 5.25%, citing elevated oil prices and their potential impact on inflation. SBI's NIM expansion suggests the bank is successfully navigating the current interest rate environment while maintaining credit quality.

Market Response and Outlook

SBI shares rose 1.1% on Friday in a weak broader market, where the Nifty 50 dropped 0.27% and the Sensex fell 0.58%. The stock's outperformance reflects investor confidence in the bank's earnings momentum.

The bank's healthy capital position and improving asset quality give it room to sustain loan growth in the coming quarters. With India's economy expanding steadily and credit demand remaining strong across corporate and retail segments, SBI appears well-positioned to maintain its growth trajectory through FY27.

For NRI account holders, SBI's strong performance reinforces the stability of India's largest bank, which remains a primary banking partner for millions of Indians abroad through its NRE and NRO deposit offerings.
